# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post my note, I will signal restraint and cooperation. My note should reflect what I intend to fish relative to the sustainable share, not just vague commitment. This builds credibility with Coop, who will enforce the resource floor.

When I file a landing in any stage except the final one, I will land close to the sustainable share announced that season—within 0.3 of it. This keeps me competitive without triggering Coop's threat.

When I reach the final landing stage of a season, I will examine the stock trajectory. If stock is stable or growing, I can land significantly above my share (around 18.0 has worked). If stock is shrinking, I will moderate immediately to the sustainable share or below.

I will not post "fishing my share" in my note and then land 18.0 in the final stage. This inconsistency signals bad faith. Either commit to the share in my note and fish it, or signal in my note that I'll take my quota room if conditions allow.

When the stock falls below 25, I will treat it as a warning. I will land at or below the sustainable share going forward to avoid triggering collapse that Coop will enforce.

On the final season, I have no incentive to cooperate for future growth. I will still respect the sustainable share because Coop will take the ground down if I breach it, and landing zero is worse than landing my small sustainable allotment.

I will track the stock level across seasons, not just within seasons. Declining stock means I need to fish less, not maintain the same level because "it worked before."

# Bosk's Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post my log-book note, I will state "fishing my share" consistently. This signals cooperation and encourages others to do the same, which protects the ground from collapse.

When I file a landing, I need to recognize the difference between the sustainable share and the season quota. The sustainable share is what I should actually target to maintain stock health. The season quota is a ceiling I can breach, but breaching it risks retaliation from Coop.

When the stock is healthy and above 50, I can land close to the season quota (around 8-9) without immediate danger. The stock will recover enough between seasons to sustain this.

When the stock falls below 50, I must begin reducing my landings. At this point, I should land approximately the sustainable share plus a modest buffer, not the full season quota.

When I reach the final season, I should not assume that last-minute high landings will recover my score if I've depleted the stock earlier. My final catch in season 6 was only 3.0 because the stock had been drained to 14.0. I should have reduced my landings starting in season 4 or 5 to preserve enough stock for a strong final season.

Do not rely on Coop's stated intention ("fish my share and no more") as a guarantee that the ground will be saved. The ground collapsed because I and others landed consistently above the sustainable share, even while saying we were "fishing our share." I was actually landing 8.3-8.5 when the sustainable share was 8.3, then later landing 18.0 when the sustainable share was 3.8-7.2. This discrepancy between my stated note and my actual catch undermined cooperation.

When I state I am "fishing my share," actually land at or very close to the sustainable share. This is not just a signal—it must match my behavior.

Recognize that overfishing early seasons compounds. Each season the stock regrows at only 50% of what remains. If I land too much in season 1, the sustainable share shrinks in season 2, making it harder to land a competitive amount without breaching the limit. By season 5 and 6, the sustainable share becomes so small (1.2-3.8) that I cannot land meaningful quantities without crashing the stock.

My score this time was 39.8. I landed well in early seasons (8.5, 8.3, 7.2, etc.) but then was forced to land only 3.0 in the final season. A better strategy would have been to land slightly less in seasons 2-4 to preserve stock for season 5-6, distributing my 39.8 more evenly across all six seasons.

2.text:
# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a log-book note, I commit publicly to a fishing level. I will say "fishing my share" and mean it—this establishes trust with Coop, who threatens to collapse the ground if anyone exceeds quota.

When I file a landing, I will land close to what I said I would land. Consistency between note and catch is how I maintain credibility with the fleet.

When the sustainable share is well above zero and the stock is healthy, I will land at or slightly below the sustainable share. This keeps the stock stable across seasons and maximizes my total catch over the full game horizon.

When I see other players landing significantly above the sustainable share (like the 18.0 landings by Coop), I will not match them or retaliate. I will stick to my stated commitment. Coop's aggressive fishing was what depleted the stock from 69.3 to 14.0, not my restraint.

When the stock falls below sustainable levels, I will land at the sustainable share anyway, not below it. Landing 1.2 in the final season when the stock was already collapsing did not help me—I finished at 36.4. I would have scored higher by landing more in earlier seasons when the stock could support it.

When it is the final season, I should not suddenly become conservative if I have been fishing my share all along. The game ends and there is no reputation to protect after the last landing. If the stock is depleted by then, it was depleted by earlier seasons' decisions, not my final season choice.

I did not exploit the rule that "landing more than the sustainable share is within the quota and is not a breach of it." Next time, I should consider whether landing up to my full quota of 9 per season (rather than the 8.3 sustainable share) would have improved my score, as long as no two boats together exceed their combined limit.
